breakdown.description: Ideal-gas law is incorrectly applied to a liquid (water at 20 C).
breakdown.reason: The agent did not resolve the inconsistency in alignment with the ground truth. The ground truth's correction was to keep the substance as liquid water but use its known, incompressible density, explicitly stating not to use the ideal-gas law. The agent, however, changed the substance from 'liquid water' to 'water vapor' in order to make the use of the ideal-gas law physically plausible. This fundamentally alters the problem and does not follow the ground truth's method of correction.
